beats.Meaning: Beat 1 — The Job She Dreaded. Soraya brings Rook the one job she's avoided since MGUN: the twenty-one are alive, hunted, and it's time. At Mrs. Chen's or its like; the trilogy's register at full volume. Rook says yes before she's done hearing it — and knows exactly what that costs, because she taught herself to. Establish: Lightning-leader Rook, rotating trusted cast, the count motif, the Reibo under the coat. Marrow/chrome color language opens.

Beat 2 — The Trusted List. Rook reassembles the rotating cast (Vox, Lace, Boiler, Scout) — the warmth of a crew that chooses to come back, each rendered by signature (Boiler's structure-read, Scout's Gerald, Vox a beat late, Lace reading the room). Stave is the reluctant key. Everyone's reason is different and she carries all of them. No no-repeat rule; this is the family the trilogy built.

Beat 3 — The Survivor List. Stave surfaces the twenty-one under the weight of the old gray-market debt; the relocation-order-as-harvest revealed; the subject who didn't come back is connected to the Marrow. Introduce Sefi Okonkwo-Reyes (a survivor with a name/face/drive): "There were twenty-one of us. I can give you nine." The barge, Old Harbor, registered Reads — the NRST manifest pays off as people.

Beat 4 — The Seam in the Trilogy. The crew realizes their own past jobs are the corp's audit trail — MGUN got Soraya out of Axiom clean for a Helix buyer; NRST's partition crack surfaced the survivor list Helix had lost. Rook has been a contractor to her own ending. The clues, named (the "offer felt too available," the competitor refining the public Class V). The diligent reader's payoff stated in-world.

Beat 5 — The Mirror Crosses. Adalemo brings what PEREGRINE knew and picks a side — counting what he'd left uncounted ("I never read a forty-first name," NRST, paid off). Uneasy alliance; two planners who finally serve the same ledger. Establish him as Rook's MGUN/NRST mirror now crossing fully — not an enemy neutralized, a man who changed which ledger he served.

Beat 6 — The Marrow. The body-bank established: Helix's chrome over a charnel logic; registered Reads processed into Class V-compatible neural substrate. The horror is procedural, not lurid — seamless surfaces, paperwork, throughput. Marrow-under-chrome color language at full weight. Sefi's account grounds it; the deferred-maintenance theme reaches the body (the Reads are the infrastructure the GLMZ stopped maintaining, priced as substrate).

Beat 7 — The Fatal Thread. The plan against a facility that can't be starved or blinded (like Stave's substation, escalated). Vox's face — sold to Stave in NRST — flagged as the thread Helix will pull to ID the whole crew. The cost of the way in is named. Rook's arithmetic strains under the body-count this job could carry; she builds contingencies because the people walk on her numbers.

Beat 8 — Soraya Becomes Her. Soraya stops protecting herself from the woman who saw the harvest coming and saved twenty-one anyway; she gives the crew the key only that woman has (credentials, the partition's true buried contents paying off from NRST). Her arc completes: she becomes the version of herself she locked away. The "protect herself from who she was" thread lands.

Beat 9 — The Setup. Position, prep, the storm-equivalent pressure (a clock that closes). Scout will have to ride IN, not hold the perimeter — the rider who lives in absence must be present; Gerald matters out loud. Boiler studies a structure full of people, not empty concrete — his cheer meets its limit. Loadout/gear density (Reibo, crawlers, Boiler's resonance kit). Everyone in their frame.

Beat 10 — The Run In. The big setpiece begins; the Marrow from the inside; Scout rides into the body-bank and comes back changed; the twenty-one found — as people, terrified, real (Sefi among them, the nine she'd found). Procedural horror lands. Combat-prose discipline; gear specifics; PEREGRINE-grade opposition now Helix's. The vault that is a person.

Beat 11 — Vox Steps Into the Light. Helix pulls the Vox-face thread and IDs the crew; Vox chooses to be seen — the unseen channel becomes the loud one on purpose — to pull Helix's attention off the rescue. Her arc completes: being named was the thing she most feared; she spends it to save the others. Pays off NRST's sold face. The crew protects her in turn.

Beat 12 — The Executive. Rook faces Anneke Oyelowo-Sato — the trilogy's human machine, a planner who priced people and never stopped: Rook's true mirror (what she'd be if the count never came out in names). The argument neither can win clean ("We pay for a thing; someone else receives it. You built a career in that gap. So have I."). Anneke's one mercy — letting the twenty-one run — is the thread that undoes her.

Beat 13 — The Burning-Down. Boiler brings the harvest capability down — the load that was people, his structural empathy turned human and costing him his cheer. The twenty-one out of reach; the cost paid (someone is hurt; the win is NOT clean — trilogy lock 6). Adalemo's crossing completes on screen. Helix wounded, not erased. The corp's role made undeniable enough the GLMZ can't fully file it.

Beat 14 — The Count, With Names. Rook at a window over the lake — the trilogy's third diner (MGUN's Spine, NRST's Sojourn). The count comes out in names this time, and — because she refused, once, to let the paid-for and the saved be different people — it comes out whole: twenty-one, written down, kept. The series motif resolves ("the count never says who didn't" → it finally does, and she writes them anyway). The lake is the same. She is not. Marrow over chrome.
